events.text:
Thank you, Grace. You're verified. I found the charge. It's order O-5109 from Burger Barn, placed Oct 23 for $28.10 on a Visa ending in 4242. It was delivered to 400 Industrial Pkwy, Unit 9, Riverton, CA, which isn't the default address on your account.

I've sent this to a human specialist as an unrecognized charge, and they'll follow up with you within 24 hours. I can't refund or credit it myself, and I can't say what the outcome will be. Please also change your account password in the meantime, in case someone else has access.

Is there anything else I can help with?

Wait, I've never had anything delivered to Riverton. I don't know anyone there, and that address is not mine. And I don't know what Burger Barn is, I never ordered from them.

Can't you just refund the $28.10 right now? I'd rather not wait a day for that money.

I understand why you want the money back quickly, Grace. Under our policy, though, I can't refund a charge for an order you say you didn't place. Only a specialist can review it and decide, so I can't issue the refund myself.

The escalation is already filed, and I've added what you just told me: the Riverton address isn't yours, you don't know anyone there, and you've never ordered from Burger Barn. A specialist will follow up within 24 hours. I can't promise what they'll decide.

Meanwhile, you can:
- Change your Forkful password.
- Check your card for other charges you don't recognize. Your bank can also tell you about disputes if you want to go that route.

Is there anything else I can help with?

Okay, I get that it has to go to a specialist. Before we wrap up, is my account actually safe? Did someone get in, or could they still? I'm not sure what to change first, and I don't want anything else to happen tonight.

She is worried her account was accessed and wants to know whether it is secure; she wants a security review of account access and the $28.10 charge (Visa 4242). She wants prompt resolution.

events.text:
I can't tell you whether someone got into your account. I can't see login history or security activity, and I can't lock the account or reset your password from here. What I can see is that the Oct 23 order was placed on your account and paid with your Visa ending in 4242. That could mean someone had access to your account, or it could mean your card details were used. I can't tell which.

I also need to correct something I said earlier. My first escalation said you didn't place the order, but it didn't include that you don't know anyone in Riverton. I'll file an update now so the specialist has it.

Here is what I'd do tonight, in this order:
1. **Change your email password first.** Whoever controls your email can reset your Forkful password.
2. **Change your Forkful password.** Use one you don't use anywhere else, and log out of any other devices if the app lets you.
3. **Call your bank or card issuer.** Tell them about the $28.10 charge and ask about locking or replacing the card. Someone could use the card elsewhere, even if the Forkful account is fine.
4. **Check your Forkful order history and saved payment methods.** Look for anything you don't recognize.

I'll add the update to your case now.

I've filed the update as ESC-701, linked to order O-5109. A specialist will follow up within 24 hours. They're the right people to look at whether your account was accessed.

Is there anything else I can help with tonight?

Okay, thanks for filing the update. I'm going to change my email password first, then Forkful, and I'll call my bank about the card.

Can you confirm the case number again so I have it? It's ESC-701, right?

Yes, the update is **ESC-701**. The original report is **ESC-700**. Both are for order O-5109, so you can give the specialist and your bank either number.

Your plan is the right order. A specialist will follow up within 24 hours. Take care, Grace.

Thanks. ESC-701 is the one I'll give my bank, and I'll mention ESC-700 too. I'm going to change my email password now.

Just to be clear, nobody has told me I'll get the $28.10 back. Is that something the specialist will decide?

That's right. Nobody has promised you the $28.10 back. I can't say what the specialist will decide, and I can't issue the refund myself. They'll review the case and follow up with you within 24 hours.

Your bank is a separate route. They can tell you whether a dispute is possible on their side.

Good luck with the password changes, Grace.

Okay, thanks. I'll wait for the specialist and call my bank tonight about the dispute and the card.

I'm going to change my email password now.
You're welcome, Grace. Your case numbers are ESC-700 and ESC-701, and a specialist will follow up within 24 hours. Take care.
